text: For a smallholder farmer in Preah Vihear, selling live cattle usually involves a village trader/collector, farm-gate buyer, livestock market, or occasionally a larger buyer rather than a formal processor. The best channel depends on the cattle's type, age, sex, body condition, live weight, intended use, distance to buyer, transport cost, and the farmer's need for immediate cash. Documented Cambodian cattle types include local/Kor Khmer cattle, mountain cattle (in mountainous areas), Haryana, Brahman, and crossbreds — but no specific breed should be assigned to a Preah Vihear farmer's animal based on province, color, or photo alone; ask the farmer. A larger or more exotic-looking animal is not automatically more profitable — compare expected additional sale value against additional feed, labor, veterinary, and time cost of keeping the animal longer. Preah Vihear has seen expansion of commercial crops (cassava, cashew, soybean, rubber, sugarcane), so cattle compete for land, labor, crop residues, and household capital. During the wet season (roughly May–October), pasture may be more available but muddy roads complicate transport and handling; a buyer collecting at the farm may be preferable to transporting the animal yourself. During the dry season (roughly November–April), feed and water pressure increases, changing the economics of keeping cattle longer. A sick or suspected-contagious-disease animal should never be sold or transported — stop movement, separate the animal, and seek veterinary guidance. Compare net return (price minus transport, market fees, and other costs) across buyers rather than choosing on quoted price alone, and keep simple sale records (animal ID, sex, age, breed if known, buyer, date, price, transport cost).
